control.body: midea control command (power, mode, target_temperature, fan_speed)
control.description: Set power / mode / target temperature / fan (msmart-ng `control`).

methods.notes: Real discovery: UDP broadcast to port 6445; devices answer and control switches to TCP 6444. See protocol_details.midea_lan_protocol.

device.manufacturer: Midea Group (many rebrands: Comfee, Inventor, Pro Breeze, Artic King, Toshiba-app units)
device.name: Midea Air Conditioner / Dehumidifier (LAN)
device.notes:
Midea's Wi-Fi air conditioners and dehumidifiers — sold under a very large number of rebrands — are controllable on the LAN over TCP port 6444 with an encrypted appliance protocol, discovered by a UDP broadcast to port 6445. Midea is a giant OEM (active); the value here is the enormous rebadge footprint plus a "one-time cloud, then local" story.
GENERATIONS:
  V1 — limited support.
  V2 — local, no token needed.
  V3 — local, but needs a TOKEN + KEY (K1) pair obtained ONCE from the Midea
       cloud (via NetHome Plus app credentials); after that, no further cloud
       connection is required.

DISCOVERY: UDP broadcast to port 6445; control then switches to TCP 6444. msmart-ng exposes Discover.discover() / discover_single(IP).
APPLIANCE TYPES: 0xAC air conditioners, 0xCC (portable), and dehumidifiers (Comfee/Inventor/Pro Breeze rebadges via midea-beautiful-air). Compatible vendor apps whose devices are reachable this way include Artic King, Midea Air, NetHome Plus, SmartHome/MSmartHome and Toshiba AC NA.
The 0x5A5A / "8370" byte-level framing is not restated here — pull it from msmart-ng source when implementing.

openness.notes: No official protocol publication. msmart-ng (a maintained fork of mac-zhou/midea-msmart) and midea-beautiful-air are the reference implementations and agree on the architecture, ports and token/key flow.

issued_to_client: V3: TOKEN + KEY (K1) pair, fetched once from the Midea cloud
credentials.notes: Wi-Fi onboarding is app-mediated (not documented here). The V3 token/key gates the encrypted TCP 6444 session; it is obtained from the cloud once and then used entirely locally.

factory_reset.effect: Returns the Wi-Fi module to onboarding (remote-control key combination on the unit). The exact gesture is model-specific and not transcribed here.

cloud.local_alternative: Yes — after a one-time cloud fetch of the V3 token/key (V2 needs none), control is entirely local over TCP 6444. The cloud is touched only to obtain the key.

methods.description: Onboard the unit onto Wi-Fi via the vendor app. For V3 firmware, retrieve the TOKEN + KEY once from the Midea cloud (NetHome Plus credentials) and cache them; all subsequent control is local over TCP 6444.

steps.action: Onboard the unit onto Wi-Fi with its vendor app.
For V3 units, fetch the token/key once from the Midea cloud (NetHome Plus credentials) and store them.
Discover on UDP 6445 and control over TCP 6444 with the cached key.

setup.notes: A device joins the LAN via its vendor app. For V3 units a token/key pair must be fetched once from the Midea cloud (using NetHome Plus credentials), after which control is fully local. V2 units need no token.

rejoin.notes: Wi-Fi re-provisioning is via the module's onboarding, not the control protocol; the cached token/key survives a network change.

testing.notes: Not driven against hardware by this project. The TCP-6444 / UDP-6445 ports, the V1/V2/V3 generation split and the one-time-cloud token/key story are from msmart-ng and midea-beautiful-air; byte-level framing should be pulled from msmart-ng source before relying on it.
